rogue.summary: The mantle is now skinned. The cap over each shoulder follows the upper arm, and the collar and the front and back panels stay on the chest. In attack2 and victory, the upper arms stay under the mantle. The dagger blades are now about 30 percent longer and 15 percent wider, with the same grip. The forge check shows result ok and ground ok, with a head margin of 0.3 cm.
strengths: In attack2, a raised arm lifts the mantle cap like a pauldron. The arm stays under the cloth, and the mantle does not tear.
The longer blades read as silver lines in the attack2 and victory sprites. The crossed daggers in the victory pose are clear from the front.
The hood, the face, the gold clasp, and the hem stitches still match the mockup, and all 8 clips are present.
issues: In attack2 at t = 0.32 s, the mantle cap over the raised arm still ends in a pointed flap. It looks like a small wing for about 0.2 s.

The top of the left bracer shows through the side of the mantle, also in the rest pose. In victory, the daggers go 0.9 cm into the mantle, and in the attack, the left dagger goes 0.6 cm into the sheath.
At 128 px the blades are still thin, and the old shape issues remain: the hood is very deep from the side, and the tunic is short and plain.
next: Round the mantle hem over the shoulders, so the lifted cap has no corner. Move the bracer in, or the mantle out, so the bracer stays under the cloth.
Move the victory cross pose 1 cm forward, and move the attack slash 1 cm away from the sheaths.

archer.summary: The archer matches the mockup well and now has the full hero clip set. The bow shot draws the string and releases a nocked arrow. The bow is still small and dark.
strengths: The attack draws the string back with a nocked arrow and then releases it. The shot reads clearly in the side view.
In the death clip, the archer staggers, falls on the back, and lies still. The bow drops to the floor next to the body.
The hood point, the elf ears, and the quiver with gold fletching give a clear silhouette in all 8 sprite directions.
issues: In the front view, the bow passes in front of the face while it rises and falls. The check shows a head margin of only 0.3 cm.
The bow and the lower string go 1.0 to 1.9 cm into the tunic and the belt in attack and attack2. The arrow is thin and dark and reads weakly.
The bow is still smaller and darker than the large recurve in the mockup. The hood rim is still thick, and the legs still look short.
next: Make the bow 20 percent larger and use a lighter wood color. This item from the last review is still open.
Move the bow path away from the face and the tunic in attack and attack2. The thinner hood rim from the last review is also still open.

knight.summary: The knight is very close to the mockup and now has the full hero clip set. The helmet, the red plume, the heart shield, and the red cape read clearly at 128 px.
strengths: Steel, gold, and red cloth read as clearly different materials in the model and in the sprites.
The clip set is complete: idle, walk, run, a sword slash, a shield bash, hit, death, and victory. The feet stay planted in the walk and the run.
The shield stays clear of the face at rest, and no held item passes through the head in any clip.
issues: In the victory clip, the raised sword reaches only the brow of the helmet. In the slash, the body hides the sword during the wind-up.
The rig has no knees. The legs stay stiff when he falls and lies on the ground in the death clip.

Small contacts remain: the left gauntlet goes up to 1.1 cm into the cuirass in the death and the shield bash. The helmet has ear discs only, not the cheek guards of the mockup. At 65,322 triangles, the knight is the heaviest model.
next: Add small cheek guards to the helmet.
Move the mail ring pattern into the normal map if the triangle count must go down.

wizard.summary: The wizard is a fire mage with a large red hat, a forked fire staff, and a flame in her left palm. The front matches the mockup well. The back and the staff are simpler than in the mockup. All 8 clips work, and every held item stays 1.2 cm or more from the head. The victory clip is now a real jump on bent knees.
strengths: The hat has a soft wavy brim, a curled tip, a brown band, and a gold flame badge. It gives her a clear silhouette in all 8 sprite directions.
In the victory clip, she crouches on bent knees with flat soles, pushes off, jumps about 8 cm with the toes down, and lands on bent knees. The staff goes up and out to her right.
In the attack clip, the staff leans out past the side lock, then drives forward at the target with a large orb flare. The staff stays 1.2 cm or more from the head.
issues: The back of the cape is one plain red area with only a gold hem. From the back and the side, the hat and the cape merge into one red mass, also at sprite size.
The staff is a thin straight pole with a small fork. In the mockup, the staff is a thick twisted branch that holds the orb. The palm flame is also smaller than in the mockup.
The long coat hides the knees, so the crouch and the landing in the victory clip and the stride in the walk are weak from the side.
next: Add a gold flame emblem and a trim band to the back of the cape.
Make the staff a thicker twisted branch that holds the orb, and make the palm flame larger.

cleric.summary: The cleric is a dwarf battle priest with a ginger mane, a braided beard, a large cross hammer, and a holy book. The front silhouette matches the mockup, and all eight clips are done. The victory is now a real jump on bent knees, with the hammer thrust at the top of the jump.
strengths: The front silhouette matches the mockup: the large octagonal hammer on the right, the big ginger head, and the book with gold corners on the left.
The attack is a clear overhead smash. The hammer rises behind the head, goes over the top, and hits the ground in front of the dwarf.
The victory has a crouch on flat feet, a push-off, a 9 cm jump with the toes down, and a landing on bent knees. The hammer is highest at the top of the jump and stays 1.1 cm or more from the head.
issues: The brows point down at the center and the eyes are large and round, so the face looks stern and young. The mockup face is older and smiles.
The side braids and their rings are short and small, so they do not show in the front view. The tunic and the tabard hide the knees, so the bent legs show only a little in the jump.
In the attack, the right bracer goes 0.9 cm into the collar and comes to 0.1 cm from the hair. The model has 85,058 triangles, the highest count of the heroes.
next: Raise the brows, make the eyes a little smaller, and add heavier lower lids, for an older and friendlier face.
Move the right arm out in the attack, so the bracer stays out of the collar and 1 cm or more from the hair.

druid.summary: The druid reads as the mushroom girl at once, and all 8 clips pass the check. The flask throw now reads clearly: the flask flies at 1.5 times its size, spins one turn, and breaks in a green splash 1 m in front. The staff, the apron, and the belt still differ from the mockup. At 76,174 triangles, she is the heaviest model in the set.
strengths: The large spotted cap with the cream rim and the gills gives a unique silhouette in every view and in all 8 sprites.
The face is very close to the mockup: large brown eyes, pink cheeks, a small smile, and a ginger bob.

Both attacks read as the druid's own. The staff cast sends a green orb at the target. The flask throw sends a large spinning flask that bursts into a green splash of 7 streaks at chest height, then the splash shrinks away.
issues: The staff is still thin and straight, and the lantern is small. The mockup staff is thick and gnarled, with a large lantern on a hook.
The front is plain. The apron is a flat card with one clover, and the three belt pouches and the small hip potion are too small to read.

The raise in the cast is low, because the wide cap blocks a staff over the head. The flask flight is fast and nearly flat, so it shows in only 2 frames of 12. At the end of the death clip, the cap stands on its rim and hides the body in the side view.
next: Make the staff thicker and gnarled, and hang a larger lantern from a hook at the top.
Make the three belt pouches and the hip potion larger, and give the apron a scalloped hem with the mushroom motif.

adventurer.summary: The adventurer is a chibi hero with a teal bandana, a red scarf, a leather harness, a short sword, a map, and a large pack with a bedroll and a lantern. It matches the mockup in the face, the clothes, the pack, and the lantern. The attack2 lunge now uses the knee bones: the right foot steps 16.6 cm forward and lands heel first, the hips drop 4 cm, and the rear heel lifts. All 9 clip lines of the forge check show ok, and the ground check shows ok.
strengths: The face reads at 128 px in the sprites: large brown eyes with highlights, rosy cheeks, and an open smile. The red scarf, the cream shirt, the harness, and the belt match the mockup.
The pack reads from all 8 sprite directions: the teal bedroll, the brass lantern on the side, and the flap with a buckle. The silhouette is clear in every view.

The attack2 lunge is a real step on the knees. The front foot lands heel first and rolls flat, the front knee bends over the foot, and the rear leg stays almost straight with the heel up. The feet stay where they land, and the sword stays more than 5 cm from the head.
issues: The front hair stands up in a spiky crown, but the mockup hair sweeps to one side. At the back and the sides, the hair is one smooth mass, like a helmet.
The legs are short, and the tunic and the large boots cover most of each leg. In the attack2 sprites, the bent front knee reads only as a lower and wider stance.
The death fall does not use the knee bones. The legs stay straight in this clip. In the attack, the hilt passes 1.1 cm from the head.
next: Solve the legs of the death fall with the knee bones, so that the knees buckle before the body falls.
Sculpt the front hair to sweep to one side as in the mockup, and add separate locks to the back and the sides of the head.

goblin-warrior.summary: The taunt hops now use the knee bones. The goblin crouches 3.4 cm on both knees, hops 7.5 cm from the right foot to the left foot, and absorbs the landing on a bent left knee. Then it hops back to the right foot and puts the left foot down. In each hop, the free leg tucks up with the knee bent and the heel up. The point, the fist on the hip, the ear flicks, the head tilt, and the dagger spin did not change. The forge check shows result ok and ground ok, and the blade stays 2.4 cm or more from the head.
strengths: The hops read in the front and side views: the body drops, the boots leave the floor, one boot tucks up, and the landing knee bends.
The broad leaf ears, the angry eyes, and the fang read at once. The face reads at 128 px in the S, SW, and SE sprites.
All identity cues of the mockup are present: the nicked ear, one shoulder guard, the diagonal strap, the pouch, the wraps, and the dagger. At 30,374 triangles, the model is light.
issues: In the taunt point, the wrist bends about 90 degrees, because the grip is across the fist. The tunic hem hides most of the knee bend, so the crouch reads as a drop of the body.
In the SW and SE sprites, the far ear still reads as a narrow point above the head.
The belt buckle is still smaller than the large tan buckle in the mockup. The pouch does not show from the back.
next: Add a second new clip (for example a block or a cheer) to get to 8 clips, as the heroes have.
Turn the ears more to the front (about 20 degrees of sweep instead of 32), and make the belt buckle about 30 percent larger.

horned-boar.summary: The horned boar is a strong chibi monster with seven clips. The new taunt is a 1.8 s snort and hoof scrape before a charge: the head drops, the boar snorts twice, and the left front hoof scrapes the floor twice. The short snout in profile is the largest open fault.
strengths: The taunt reads as a threat. The head drops so the horns tilt forward, the weight shifts back, and the tail rises and lashes. Two snorts jerk the head up and make the body shudder.
The taunt scrape uses the same two-bone IK as the attack. The hoof lifts, sets down ahead, and draws back on its toe along the floor. The other three hooves stay planted and flat.
The attack has clear stages: a low gather, a 0.2 m charge, and a hooked toss. The shin fur ends inside the hooves, so the raised soles in the death show solid black discs.
issues: The snout is still short in profile. In the side view and in the W and E sprites, the snout is only a small pink edge, and the head looks flat.
The snorts in the taunt are small. At 128 px the head jerk is hard to see, and the ears have no bones, so they do not flick.
When the head is low in the attack, the lower jaw goes into the front of the chest. From the side, the head and the chest merge into one mass.
next: Make the snout 20 percent longer. A longer snout gives a boar profile in the side view, the W and E sprites, and the attack.
Give the ears their own bones, so the taunt, the hit, and the idle can flick them.

goblin-archer.summary: The goblin archer has a new taunt clip. The goblin shakes the bow high out to the side and hops from foot to foot two times. Then it turns, holds the bow up in front, plucks the empty string once, and grins at the player. The full clip set is idle, walk, run, a bow shot, hit, death, and taunt. The hood, the ears, the face, and the leather gear match the mockup.
strengths: The pointed dark hood with the ears through it gives a strong, unique silhouette in every view and in every sprite direction.
The taunt reads at a distance. The raised bow shakes beside the head, the feet lift in the two hops, and the string pulls back and snaps in the pluck.
The bow and the arms stay clear of the head in every clip. In the taunt, the bow turns so the string is in front of the limbs and not against the hood. The closest part comes to 1.1 cm from the hood.
issues: The short arms and the big hood keep the raised bow low. The fist stays at chin height, and the bow top rises only to the ear tips, not above the hood peak.
In the taunt, the bracer tops touch the capelet hem by 0.1 cm when the arms are up, as in the shot. The body turn for the pluck repeats the shot's nock, so the pluck looks a little like a shot.
The ears are thin flat plates. The model has no long back cape and no chest strap from the mockup. In the draw and the pluck, the lower string touches the capelet by 0.9 cm.
next: Give the pluck its own hold with less body turn, so it reads less like the shot's nock.
Give the ears thickness and a cupped inner face, and add the long back cape and the chest strap from the mockup.

skeleton.summary: The skeleton warrior matches the enemy-sheet design: a grinning skull with glowing eyes under a riveted helmet, a red scarf, mail, a sword, and a round red shield. A new spawn clip, rise, starts on the last frame of the death heap. The bones rattle, the skull rolls back and hops onto the neck, the torso and the legs come up, and the sword and the shield fly into the hands. The forge check shows result ok and ground ok. The helmet is still dark iron.
strengths: The rise clip starts exactly on the death end pose and ends exactly on the rest pose. The order is clear: a beat, a rattle, the skull roll and hop, the sit-up, the stand-up, the catch of the sword and the shield, and a double nod.
The chop has a clear wind-up, hold, cut, and follow-through. The blade stays about 3 cm clear of the helmet, and the shield arm tucks out of the blade path.
The slanted black sockets, the amber eyes, and the square teeth make a clear angry skull face. Iron, mail, bone, red cloth, wood, and brass read as different materials.
issues: In the rise heap, the huge helmet hides most of the body in the three-quarter view, and the rattle is small. The rattle shows mostly on the skull, the sword, and the scarf.
The helmet is still dark iron all over. The mockup shows lighter steel with dark patches. From above, the dark dome is the largest shape in the sprites.
The model stands in a neutral pose, but the mockup shows a lunge. The mockup has brown leather boots; the model has plain steel feet.
next: Make the helmet steel lighter, with the patina in patches. This item from the old review is still open.
Give the rest pose a small lunge and brown leather boots, as in the mockup.

orc-warrior.summary: The orc warrior is a stocky brute with a heavy scowl, tusks, a topknot, a spiked pauldron, and a large crescent axe. A new second attack, attack2, is a shoulder charge with the spiked pauldron and then a backhand axe swipe. The orc turns the pauldron shoulder to the target, takes two heavy steps, and rams at chest height. Then the body unwinds and the axe swings across at waist height with the edge in front. The clip check passes the head test and the ground test for all clips.
strengths: The second attack reads clearly: the spiked pauldron leads the charge, and the head stays low behind it.
The feet stay on the floor in the charge: each planted foot keeps its position, and the hips move over the feet.
The costume matches the mockup: large brown bracers, a spiked pauldron, a belt with a round buckle, a ragged red loincloth, and fur leg wraps.
issues: In the charge, the axe hangs low across the front, and the axe head comes near the floor.
The tusks are small: about half the size of the mockup tusks. They hang down from under the upper lip, as the owner asked.
The beard is a small goatee, and the mockup beard is full.
next: Hold the axe higher in the charge of attack2, so that the head of the axe stays clear of the feet.
Give the beard more volume, toward the full beard of the mockup.

bandit.summary: The bandit has a new taunt clip for the first sight of the player. He leans back with the head cocked and beckons twice with the free hand, palm up. Then he tosses the cutlass, it turns one full flip, and he catches it. Then he points the blade at the player. The full clip set is now idle, walk, run, a cutlass slash, hit, death, and taunt. The gear is still plainer than the mockup.
strengths: The taunt reads as one attitude: a cocky beckon, a trick toss, and a threat. The cutlass rises beside the head, turns one full flip in 0.35 s, and drops back into the hand at the same grip.
The cutlass stays 5 cm or more from the head and the hair in the taunt. The head tilts away from the toss and turns to watch it. The check ends with result ok and ground ok.
The glare between the dark hair and the red mask is a strong focal point. It reads in the front view and in the S, SW, and SE sprites.
issues: The hand is a closed fist, so the beckon shows as a fist that tilts up twice. The fingers do not curl, and in the side views the far hand is hidden.
In the front view and the S sprite, the pointed blade faces the camera and shows only as a short curve. The point reads better in the W, E, and SE sprites.
The gear is plainer than the mockup. The mockup has straps on the vest, a holster at the belt, and tall boots with cuffs. The model has a plain vest and short boots.
next: Give the free hand an open pose for the beckon: a palm with fingers that curl, on its own bone, used only in the taunt.
Add the mockup gear: a vest strap with a buckle, a holster at the belt, and cuffs on the boots.

zombie.summary: A new spawn clip, rise (2.0 s), is added. The zombie starts bent forward below the floor, with only the left hand above it. The hand bursts up and claws, the right hand follows, and both hands slam down flat on the floor. The body comes up in three jerky heaves, stands, shudders, and groans. The hair, the shirt, and the trouser hems are still simpler than the mockup.
strengths: The rise reads clearly: a clawing hand, a second hand, a push on the floor, three heaves, and a stand. The pushing hands stay flat on the floor at y 0 to 4 cm and do not slide.
The bulging yellow eye and the glossy black eye read in every sprite direction that shows the face.
The attack, the walk, the run, and the death read as a zombie at once: one foot drags, the arms stay forward, and the fall ends flat on the ground.
issues: In the rise, the hips start only 0.5 m below the floor, because the short chibi arms cannot reach the floor from deeper. The raised hand comes up only about 18 cm above the floor.
The rise sprites and the review strips show the full body below the floor. Only a game floor at y = 0 hides it; the sprite renderer does not cut the body at the floor.
The hair is still a smooth black helmet with thick cone locks, and the shirt is still plain, with no torn collar, buttons, or loose threads.
next: Make the hair locks thinner and more varied, and break up the smooth mass at the back.
Let the sprite renderer cut a clip at y = 0 when the clip sets ground: false, so the rise sprites show only the part above the floor.

slime.summary: The slime is a glossy green jelly dome on a lobed puddle base, with three floating bubbles. The body and the face match the slime king mockup without the crown, the cape, and the chain. A new spit clip gives the slime a ranged attack: it squashes wide, squints, stretches tall, and spits an acid glob about 1 m forward in an arc. The attack is a leap with a hard splat, and the death melts the jelly into a puddle.
strengths: The spit clip reads in three clear stages: a wide squash with swollen cheeks and squinting eyes, a fast stretch up and forward, and a jiggle back to rest. The core never moves, so the slime does not slide.

The acid glob uses the SLIME color with more saturation, so the fire, ice, and poison variants get a matching glob. It flies 1 m in a 0.3 s arc, wobbles, and is hidden inside the body in every other clip.
The face reads at 128 px in the S sprite: big white eyes with lime irises, heavy brow ridges, and a frown. No clip goes below the ground (ground ok).
issues: The acid glob is 7.4 cm across, so it is only a few pixels in the 128 px spit sprites, and it leaves the sprite cell in the second half of its flight.
The mouth paint stays on the jelly, so the melted puddle shows a thin dark line at its front rim. The puddle also shows faint radial streaks on its top.
In the front view, a vertical ridge above the small frown reads as a nose. In the side view, the eye white sticks out of the profile as a white disc.
next: Add a small acid splat on the ground where the glob lands, or a brighter glow on the glob, so the spit reads at sprite size.
Hide the frown in the death puddle, remove the nose ridge, and set the eyes a little deeper into the dome.

dire-wolf.summary: The wolf has a new clip, howl (2.0 s, one shot). The wolf takes a breath: the chest swells and lifts, the rear sinks, and the head dips. Then the head tips far back with the nose to the sky, the jaw opens 30 degrees, and the tail rises. The howl holds 0.8 s with a tremble in the jaw and the head. Then the head comes down, the jaw closes, the head shakes, and the wolf goes back to rest. The model and the other clips did not change.
strengths: The howl pose reads in all 8 sprite directions at 128 px: the open jaw and the raised muzzle show clearly in the front and three-quarter views.
The front paws stay in place. The hips move comes from the front leg chain, and each hind leg is solved so its heel stays on the ground.
The chest swell scales only the chest: the front legs and the neck cancel the spine scale, so the head and the paws keep their size.
issues: The ears are part of the head fur and have no bone, so they do not fold back in the howl. They only turn with the head.
In the breath and the howl, the hind toes lift about 1 cm because the bent hind leg tilts the rigid paw on the heel.
The legs are straight and the side view is longer than the compact mockup. The hit and the death do not open the jaw.
next: Add ear bones (ear.L and ear.R) and fold the ears back in the howl and the hit.
Open the jaw in the hit (a yelp) and a little in the death, so all clips use the jaw.

giant-spider.summary: The giant spider is close to the mockup in the front view and reads clearly as a sprite. A new spit clip gives it a ranged web attack: it rocks back, curls the abdomen up, jerks forward, and a web glob flies 1 m forward from between the fangs. The attack drive and the fang snap are still open.
strengths: The big eyes match the mockup: a bright white eyeball with a red iris about half the eye wide, a small dark pupil, and a highlight.
The spit reads in the side and three-quarter strips: the head tips up and the fangs spread, then a sharp jerk forward, and the glob flies 1 m with its strands behind it.
All eight feet stay planted in the spit, and the web glob stays hidden inside the head in every other clip and in the rest pose.
issues: The web glob is only about 5.5 cm across. At 128 px it is a few white pixels in flight, so the spit reads mostly from the body motion.
The abdomen curl in the spit is 38 degrees. From the front and the three-quarter views the head hides most of it; only the side view shows it clearly.
The forward drive in the attack stops at 16 cm, and the fang snap is hard to see from the side, because the low head hides the fangs at the bite.
next: Check the spit sprite sheet at 128 px. If the glob does not read, make it larger in flight or add a short web trail.
Check the fang snap in a front view of the attack, and open the fangs wider at the top of the rear-up if it does not read.

dragon-fire.summary: The fire dragon matches the mmx mockup closely in shape and color: a squat red dragon that is half head, with cream horns, a crest, heavy black brows, a toothy grin, orange bat wings, and a ridged cream belly. The attack is a fire-breath roar with a jaw bone and a level cone of fire. A new roar clip (1.8 s) makes the dragon rear up with the wings and the claws raised, open the jaw 40 degrees with a small puff of fire at the lips, shake the head, and drop back with a stomp.
strengths: The spread wings, the horns, and the crest make a unique silhouette that reads in all eight sprite directions.
The roar has clear stages: a rear-up with a full chest, a head thrust with the jaw wide open, a shaking hold, and a forward stomp with a chest squash. The hind feet stay exactly on their rest spots.
The jaw splits along the painted grin, so the closed mouth looks the same as before. The open mouth shows a dark throat, a tongue, and the lower teeth.
issues: The fire cone and the roar puff read as smooth orange shapes. They have only a small scale flicker, no glow, and no smoke.
In the roar, the raised wings stand almost upright, so from the front they look narrower than the rest pose. The front claws cannot reach the ground, so the stomp reads mostly through the body pitch.
In the three-quarter view, the death ends with the head and the belly as two separate blobs, and the face lies sideways.
next: Give the fire more life: two or three flame tongues with their own flicker, a yellow core, and a short smoke puff when the breath ends.
Open the jaw in the hit and in the death roar, and fix the three-quarter end pose of the death.

blacksmith.summary: The blacksmith matches the mmx mockup in costume and color: a red bandana, a black beard, a leather bib apron with brass rings, big gloves, and a hammer at the right shoulder. The work clip now has tongs in the left fist and a glowing hot billet in the jaws. The hammer face lands flat on the billet at the blow, and the billet flashes. The body is still less burly than the mockup. The check ends with result ok and ground ok.
strengths: The red bandana, the black beard, and the brown apron read at 128 px in all 8 sprite directions.
Dark iron tongs with a rivet and flat jaw pads come out of the left fist. The orange-red billet glows and is easy to see in the side and three-quarter views.
The billet stays still in the world during the loop. The clip samples at 50 frames each second, so a key falls exactly on the blow and the face touches the billet top.
issues: The head is still larger than the torso. In the mockup, the chest and the arms are larger than the head, so the model is less burly than the mockup.
There is no anvil. The billet hangs in the air at thigh height (y 0.16) in front of the belly, held only by the tongs.
The soot mark under the left eye is dark blue-gray and reads as a bruise in the front sprites. The back hair is one plain black mass.
next: Make the chest, the shoulders, and the arms 10 percent bigger. This item from the last three reviews is still open.
Add a small anvil prop or a scene anvil under the billet (about x 0.02, y 0.15, z 0.47) so the blow hits a real surface.

farmer.summary: The farmer model matches the mmx mockup well: a wide straw hat, a straw bundle in the mouth, a red plaid shirt, patched blue overalls, and a tall pitchfork. The work clip now uses the knee bones: the hips drop 6 cm on bent knees with flat feet, and the stab tilts the fork 47 to 49 degrees down. The face stays clear of the brim in every frame.
strengths: The wide straw hat and the tall pitchfork make a silhouette that reads as a farmer at once, also in the 128 px sprites.
The stab drives the fork 47 to 49 degrees down with both hands on the haft, and the tines go at most 11 cm into the soil. The fork stays 2.2 cm or more from the head.
The legs bend at the knees with the soles flat in a wide stance, and the knees straighten again for the lift and the toss.
issues: The legs are very short, so the knee bend is small in the side view: the overalls hide most of it.
At the toss the left fist moves up to 4.6 cm off the haft axis, and in the draw up to 2.3 cm, because the short arms cannot reach the fork across the chest.
The haft goes up to 0.9 cm into the shirt and the overalls in the lift, the toss, and the return. The stab and the lever are clear.
next: Let the left hand slide along the haft at the toss (a larger gap key), so the fist stays on the haft axis.
Give the return path a little more room from the shirt, for example a wider yaw at phase 0.84 to 0.96.

guard.summary: The spear thrust is now a lunge. The front foot steps 0.19 m forward, the hips drop 4 cm, and the rear heel rises. The spear tip travels 0.40 m along the aim line in 0.1 s and holds 0.1 s. The strip shows a clear drive.
strengths: The lunge and the long drive read clearly in the side view.
The feet stay planted: the front foot lands with the hips, and the rear foot rolls on its sole edge.
The front foot lifts when it steps back, and the hips rise a little on the rear foot.
issues: Both forearms go 2 to 3 cm into the mail at full extension, because the short arms reach across the chest.
The right gauntlet comes 1.0 cm from the face at full extension.
The rigid legs make a wide, flat lunge; there is no knee to bend.
next: Keep the forearms off the mail at full extension, for example with a spear line further in front of the chest.
Make 3 color variants after all clips are done.

skeleton-mage.summary: The skeleton mage matches the candle-skull caster on the mockup. A new taunt clip (1.6 s) plays when the mage first sees the player. The skull tips back and bobs four times in a cackle, the eyes pulse, and the palm flame rises beside the skull and swells to 1.5 times its size. Then the flame hand points at the player for a beat. All 7 clips pass the head check and the ground check. The model has 43,728 triangles.
strengths: The candle on the skull is a unique silhouette. It shows clearly in all 8 sprite directions.
The taunt cackle reads at 128 px in all 8 directions: the skull and the candle tip back, and the large purple flame rises beside the skull.
The cast and the death are clear: a flare and a bolt in the cast; a collapse, a falling staff, a rolling skull, and lights that go out in the death.
issues: The point in the taunt is weak from the front: the hand moves toward the camera, and the forward skull tilt hides part of the face.
In the idle, the staff comes to 0.5 cm from the wax on the skull. It passes the check, but the margin is small. In the taunt, the margin is 1.5 cm.
The candle is a wide block with a flat top, and the skull has no hood. The mockup has a taller, rounder candle and a dark hood.
next: Make the candle taller and rounder, and add a dark hood behind the skull, as on the mockup.
Tilt the staff out a little more in the idle, so that it stays 1 cm or more from the wax.

imp.summary: The imp matches the imp on the Chibi Quest enemy sheet. It is a big-headed red devil with dark horns, amber eyes, fangs, bat wings, claws, and a spade tail. A new clip, cast (1.2 s), throws a fireball. The imp rises and leans back, a small orange fireball grows between its hands, and then the imp lunges and pushes the ball out. The ball flies 1 m forward at chest height in 0.2 s. The flat light membranes and the thin leading bone remain open.
strengths: The spread bat wings and the curved horns give a spiky silhouette that reads in all eight sprite directions.

The attack has three clear parts. The imp rises with the claws beside the head and the wings up, dives forward with a hard downstroke, holds both claws at full forward reach for 0.12 s, and rakes down.
The cast has a clear gather, throw, and recovery. The wing beat runs the whole time, the lunge falls on the downstroke, and the ball stays 4 cm or more from the head.
issues: In the cast, the fireball is only 5.6 cm across. At 128 px the gather shows as a few orange pixels between the hands, and the ball in flight is a small dot.
The membranes are one flat light orange (#e0704a), lighter than the skin, with sharp star points. The mockup membranes are darker red-orange with rounded scallops.
The leading bone is dark and thick only to the knuckle. From the knuckle to the top tip it is a thin finger.
next: Darken the membranes toward the wing tips with C.membraneDark and carry the thick dark leading bone from the knuckle to the top wing tip.
Make the cast read at 128 px: let the fireball flare to 1.5 times its size at the release, or add a short flame trail in flight.

skeleton-archer.summary: A new clip, taunt (1.7 s, one shot), plays when the archer first sees the player. The right hand takes an arrow from the quiver and holds it up beside the hood, out to the right. The skull tips back and bobs four times in a rattling laugh, and the shoulders shake. Then the bow comes forward and the arrow taps the upper limb once. The arrow goes back into the quiver. The model and the other clips did not change. The check passes (result ok, ground ok).
strengths: The taunt reads in the front view: the arrow up beside the hood, the skull tipped back, then the arrow across the bow.
The arms move by targets: the arrow nock, the bow contact point, and the quiver come from the rig, so the shaft touches the front of the bow limb at the tap.
The held items stay 2.6 cm or more from the hood and the skull in the taunt, and the mantle caps follow the upper arms.
issues: The four laugh bobs are fast (about 9 per second), so the 12-frame strip shows only the tipped-back skull, not each bob.
The tap is small (about 5 cm of travel); at 128 px it reads more as a gesture across the bow than as a hit.
Old small lines remain: the red wraps go 0.9 cm into the mantle in the taunt and the attack, and the arrow goes 0.3 cm into the quiver when the hand takes it.
next: Give the tap a small bow recoil at the contact so the hit reads in the sprites.
Keep the red wraps out of the mantle hem when the right arm crosses the chest.

giant-rat.summary: The giant rat matches the front of its mmx mockup: round pink-lined ears, red eyes under angry brows, a pink nose, buck teeth, head spikes, back tufts, a red neckerchief, and a ringed tail. A new taunt clip is a threat squeal: the rat rears up on its toes, spreads its claws, squeals with the jaw open, shakes, and chatters its teeth.
strengths: The round ears, the head spikes, the back tufts, and the long tail give a clear silhouette from every side and in all 8 sprite directions.
The taunt reads well in the front view: the hips rise 6.5 cm on rolled toes, the claws spread wide at chest height, the jaw opens 35 degrees for 0.5 s, and the jaw snaps shut twice.
The attack has a crouch, a 15 cm dart with a step, a claw rake, and a snap with a nod down. IK keeps the feet planted in the attack and in the taunt.
issues: In the side view, the snout is still short and flat, and the body stands upright. The sides and the belly are smooth, with no fur clumps or folds.
The ears and the whiskers have no bones. In the taunt, only small head turns make them twitch. The fast body shake is small at sprite size.
The tail slides 15 cm on the ground with the hips during the dart. The hit and the death clips do not use the jaw.
next: Push the snout and the nose 0.03 m forward, and lean the chest and the head forward. Add fur clumps along the sides and belly folds in the paint.
Use the jaw in the other clips: a squeal with the mouth open in the hit, a small chew in the idle sniff, and a slack jaw in the death.

giant-bat.summary: The giant bat matches the front of its mmx mockup: a round purple fur ball, tall ears, yellow eyes under heavy brows, a pink snout, fangs, and pink wings. A new screech clip adds a threat display: the bat pulls back, spreads its wings, and screeches with a wide open jaw.
strengths: The screech clip reads well: the bat pulls back nose up, the wings freeze raised and spread, the ears prick forward, and the jaw opens 40 degrees for 0.6 s.
During the screech, the ball puffs up 8 percent and shakes fast, and the tongue and the lower fangs show in the open mouth.
The attack, the idle, the hit, and the death still read well. No clip sinks below the ground, and the build gives no warnings.
issues: The open lower jaw looks ragged in close views: its top face is dark to the lip edge, and the chin fur spikes cover part of the lower lip.
The ears are still tall pointed triangles with a straight rim.
In the side view and in the W and E sprites, the wings are still thin pink fins beside the ball.
next: Round the ear outline and add two or three scallops to its back edge.
Angle the wings 20 degrees toward the front at rest, so they read in the side view and in the W and E sprites.

mimic.summary: The mimic matches its mmx mockup and uses the planks, iron, and gold lock of the treasure chest asset. The open lid is a jaw of white fangs with yellow slit eyes. Red flesh, a purple tongue, and iron claw feet complete it. This pass changed the attack clip. The chest rears back, hops 0.22 m forward, and leans 12 degrees into the bite. The lid stops 15 degrees open, so the fangs interlock at the seam at full size. The chest holds the bite for 0.1 s with a small shake, lets go, and returns to rest. The lower corner fangs moved 4 cm inward, so they stand inside the upper corner fangs and do not touch them.
strengths: The bite now shows the fangs: at the contact frame the lower teeth stand in front of the lid and the upper corner fangs dip inside the lower lip.
Closed (the first frame of the reveal clip), the mimic matches the real treasure chest, so the trap works in a level.
The death reads well. The chest shivers and gapes, the front legs buckle, then the back legs, and the lid falls shut on the limp tongue.
issues: At 128 px, the fangs at the bite are small white marks. The bite reads best in the S, SW, and SE sprites and is weak in the side sprites.
The mockup shows gold coins and cloth in the flesh; the model has only flesh. The teeth are still straight cones with thin bases.
The chest body is a square box; the mockup chest flares out toward the top. The iron bands are blue-black; the mockup iron is a warm dark gray-brown.
next: Add a few gold coins and a gem in the flesh, from the treasure heap of the chest. This item from the old review is still open.
Make the tooth bases thicker and bend the middle teeth a little toward the front, so the bite reads more strongly at 128 px.

animated-armor.summary: The animated armor matches its mmx mockup: a huge round great helm with a brass band, a black visor with two cyan eyes, and a slotted face plate. This pass changed only the attack clip. In the wind-up, the sword arm now goes straight out to the side, below the cheek plate, and the elbow points out. The blade stands up beside the helm, so the front view shows the top of the backswing. The fist passes 3.5 cm below the cheek plate when it comes forward. The edge leading, the diagonal cut, the low-left follow-through, the step, and the recovery did not change. ./forge check gives result ok and ground ok.
strengths: The front view now shows the whole slash: the blade stands up beside the helm, then cuts across the front to the low left.
The sword fist stays 3.5 cm or more from the helm at every frame of the attack.
The wrist and the blade follow keys with reach, orient, and edgeUp, so the clip is a clean worked example for other assets.
issues: In the three-quarter view, the top of the backswing is still behind the helm.
The awaken rattle is short and small, so it is hard to see at sprite size.
The cheek flare is small, so the cheek plates read weakly from the side.
next: Look at the attack and awaken sprite sheets at 128 px and make the rattle larger if it does not show.
Flare the cheek plates more, and keep the attack fist 1 cm or more below them.

innkeeper.summary: A new settlement NPC on the farmer base (the shared rogue head, skeleton, and knee bones). The hair bun with the white bow, the swept bangs, the sage-green dress with cream cuffs and collar, the white apron, and the tray with a foaming tankard match the mockup. The work clip is now a serving motion with the tray kept level. The forge check shows result ok, and the textured build has no warnings.
strengths: The silhouette and colors read as the mockup at a glance: bun, bow, green dress, white apron, and tray.
The tray stays level in every clip through one helper, and the serving work clip suits the role.
Color options for the dress stay in tavern dyes (green, wine, walnut, ochre) with three presets.
issues: The lower edge of the apron shows a small speckle where it meets the skirt pleats.
The tankard and tray are smaller than the very large tankard in the mockup.
The smile is smaller than the wide grin in the mockup, and the bangs look a little like a helmet.
innkeeper.next: Fix the apron speckle, make the tankard about 20 percent larger if the head clearance allows, and widen the smile.

shopkeeper.summary: A new settlement NPC on the farmer base (the shared rogue head, skeleton, and knee bones). The plum beret with its bow, the round spectacles, the mustache, the mustard shirt with the teal vest and brass buttons, the leather apron with pockets, and the coin pouch match the mockup closely. The work clip is now weighing the coin pouch. The forge check shows result ok, and the textured build has no warnings.
strengths: Every main feature of the mockup is present and in the right place, from the beret bow to the apron pockets.
The spectacles and mustache give a clear, friendly merchant face.
The beret is the clothing slot (plum, faded indigo, mustard ochre, olive) with three presets: jeweler, grocer, spicer.
issues: The beret is a stronger violet than the soft lavender-plum of the mockup, and its rim is thinner.
The mustache is small at 128 px; the nose and the high sprite camera hide part of it.
The right arm holds the pouch out to the side; the mockup holds it more to the front.
shopkeeper.next: Soften the beret toward lavender-plum, enlarge the mustache about 25 percent, and bring the pouch arm forward.

villager.summary: A new settlement NPC on the farmer base (the shared rogue head, skeleton, and knee bones). The moss headscarf, the curly pigtails, the rose dress with puffed sleeves, the cream apron with a back bow, and the basket of bread in the left hand match the mockup. The work clip lifts and settles the basket. The forge check shows result ok, and the textured build has no warnings.
strengths: The headscarf, pigtails, dress, apron, and basket read clearly at 128 px in all eight directions.
The dress is the clothing slot with earthy options (rose, faded indigo, moss, rust brown) and three presets, so a crowd of villagers looks varied.
The basket stays clear of the hair in every clip (closest 1.7 cm in run).
issues: The ruffled apron hem shows a small speckle, the same fault as on the innkeeper.
The mockup has a longer torso and legs; the chibi base shows less leg between skirt and socks.
The pigtails point out to the sides more than the hanging coils of the mockup, and the moss dress option is close to the moss scarf.
villager.next: Fix the apron hem speckle (shared with the innkeeper), let the pigtails hang lower, and move the moss dress option away from the scarf color.

quest-giver.summary: A new settlement NPC on the farmer base (the shared rogue head, skeleton, and knee bones): an elder with a blue hood and gold trim, a big white beard and brows, an open coat over a plum tunic, a twisted staff, and a scroll with a red seal. The work clip is now give, which holds the scroll out toward the viewer. The forge check shows result ok, and the textured build has no warnings. A second pass reshaped the hood: the crown sits closer to the skull and the back drapes into a short cape over the shoulders (skinned to the chest), and the nose is 25 percent larger and more peach.
strengths: From the front, the hood, beard, coat, staff, and sealed scroll read as the mockup elder.
The give clip is a clear quest hand-over with the seal turned to the viewer.
The hood and coat are the clothing slot (indigo, moss, rust, oatmeal) with three presets: hermit, reeve, scribe.
issues: From the side and back the hood is still a tall teardrop, a little larger than in the mockup.
The eyes are the large chibi eyes; the nose is larger now but still close to the skin color.
The leather shoulder straps are missing, the scroll is small, and the staff top is a plain knob.
quest-giver.next: Soften the hood tip, lower the crown a little more, and add the shoulder straps.

deer.summary: A new P0 wildlife animal on the dire-wolf quadruped rig: a chibi fawn with a big round head, glossy eyes in cream patches, pink-lined leaf ears, small two-tine antlers, a white bib, white back spots, and an upright tail. Clips: idle, walk, run (prancing), graze, alert, hit, and death. The ground check passes, and the textured build has no warnings.
strengths: The face, ears, antlers, bib, spots, and tail match the mockup closely and read at 128 px.
graze and alert replace the wolf attack and howl with deer behaviour; the ears have their own bones.
Fur and eye variants in natural colors with three presets: roe, winter, pale.
issues: The body is a little longer and taller than the short, round body of the mockup.
The antlers are thinner than the knobbly mockup antlers.
In graze, the short neck makes the antlers point forward almost level with the ground.
deer.next: Shorten and round the body a little and thicken the antlers.

horse.summary: A new P0 wildlife animal on the dire-wolf quadruped rig: a chibi chestnut horse with a white blaze, a leather halter, a cream muzzle, white socks, dark hooves, and a full mane and tail with a mane bone. Clips: idle, walk (four beats), run (gallop), rear, neigh, hit, and death. The ground check passes, and the textured build has no warnings. About 1.2 m to the ear tips, so a hero can ride it later.
strengths: The blaze, halter, muzzle, socks, and mane read as the mockup horse.
rear and neigh replace the wolf attack and howl; three clips keep the lowest point on the ground each frame.
Coat variants (chestnut, bay, dun, grey, black), mane and eye options, and four presets.
issues: In the side view the eye bulges out beyond the head outline.
The head is a little small for the body compared with the mockup.
The mane is a tall ridge of locks from the side (the mockup mane is lower and softer), and the tail is thinner.
horse.next: Sink the eyes into the head so the side outline is smooth, enlarge the head about 10 percent, and lower the mane.

ghost.summary: A new P1 dungeon denizen for the Sunken Vault on the imp hover rig: a chibi ghost with a pale egg head, big dark hollow eyes with glowing cyan pupils, a small smile, stubby arms, a wavy eight-lobed sheet hem, and a curled tail. Clips: idle, walk, attack (boo lunge), hit, death (spins down into a puddle), and taunt. The ground check passes, and the textured build has no warnings.
strengths: The silhouette, eyes, and hem match the mockup closely and read at 128 px.
The glowing pupils keep their cyan hue (dark base color under the emission).
Body and eye variants (pale, mint, lavender, grey; cyan, green, violet) with three presets.
issues: The arms cannot go fully up because the big head is in the way, so the boo pose is mild.
A very faint line shows on the sheet at y about 0.17 where the sheet is split between two bones.
The body is paler and bluer than the mint of the mockup.
ghost.next: Hide the sheet seam, and try a mint default body color.

mummy.summary: Mummy on the zombie base, reworked 2026-09-30 by a Sonnet 5.5 high-tier agent (75,483 tokens): a small linen bundle with one glowing yellow eye in a dark face hole, arms hanging at rest, a V of wrap ends at the collar, looser varied chest wraps, and two free hanging ends.
strengths: The eye is a bright yellow point in a dark hole in every front-facing sprite.
The hanging arms and the loose wraps match the mockup's pose and layering.
27,216 triangles, no warnings, ground check ok.
issues: The face hole is glossy and larger than the mockup's.
The hanging ends are thin at 128 px.
The head wraps are more regular than the mockup's loose layers.
next: Matte the face hole (roughness 0.9) and shrink it 10 percent.
Thicken the two hanging ends.

kobold-warrior.summary: A new P1 dungeon denizen on the goblin-warrior base (knee bones, enemy clips): a rust-orange scaly kobold with a long toothy snout, yellow eyes, small ivory horns, frill ears, a cream belly, a three-bone swaying tail, a battered leather vest with straps, and a crude barbed spear with a rag. The attack is a spear thrust; the taunt thumps the spear butt. The forge check shows result ok, and the textured build has no warnings.
strengths: The snout, horns, frill ears, vest, spear, and tail read as the mockup kobold.
Worley scales in paint and bump give a rich surface.
Scale, eye, and vest variants with three presets: swamp, deep, dune.
issues: Heavy angry lids make the eyes small yellow dots at 128 px; the mockup eyes are big and open.
The shoulder pads are round domes; the mockup pads are flat, wide, embossed plates.
The texture bake is slow (208 s) because of the per-texel Worley scales.
kobold-warrior.next: Open the eyes wider with bigger pupils and flatten the shoulder pads.

minotaur-guard.summary: Minotaur guard reworked 2026-09-30 by Sonnet 5.5 high-tier agents (three launches, about 66,000 tokens on the pass that finished): thick low crescent horns, a round fluffy mane, a chunky fur loincloth with leather flaps, iron pauldrons and chest plate, a brass nose ring, and one two-handed maul held low. 57,358 triangles, no warnings, check ok with no body contact.
strengths: The horn crescents read as a wide silhouette in all eight sprite directions.
The maul clears the plate, bracer, and mane in both attacks.
Fur, iron, leather, and horn read as four materials.
issues: The horns are ivory and pointed; the mockup's are rounder grey-and-cream crescents.
The mane is a smooth puff, not layered locks.
The eyes are red, not brown; the face is smaller than the mockup's.
next: Paint a grey gradient on the horn bases.
Add three lock strands to the mane.

lich.summary: The P1 boss of the Sunken Vault on the skeleton-mage base, scaled to about 1.1 m: a skull with glowing green eye lights (dark base color), pointed bony ears, a five-point gold crown with green gems, a deep purple robe with gold trim, a high collar and a gold-lined cape, and a staff with a four-talon claw holding a glowing green gem, green flames, and two wisps. attack is a new staff-raise spell; cast keeps the palm bolt; death drops the skull with its crown. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The crown, glowing eyes, robe, and gem staff read as the mockup lich and as a boss.
One eyes slot also colors the gem, flames, wisps, crown gems, and bolt, so the presets change the whole magic color.
Presets: frost-lich, blood-lich, shadow-lich.
issues: The skull is a little small for the body; the mockup head is larger and rounder with glow rings around the sockets.
The staff stands upright; in the mockup it is slanted with the gem at eye level, and the free hand is raised beside the head.
The crown points are taller and thinner than in the mockup, and the gold hem breaks into pieces between the ragged notches.
lich.next: Enlarge the skull about 10 percent, add glow rings to the sockets, and lower and broaden the crown points.

skeleton-knight.summary: A new P1 dungeon enemy on the skeleton base (knee bones, seven clips): a skeleton in a dented iron helmet with a red plume, a breastplate with a strap, pauldrons, vambraces, greaves, a torn dark red tabard, cape, and scarf, a notched sword, and a battered kite shield. hit is now a shield block. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The helmet, plume, skull, armor, and red cloth read as the mockup knight at 128 px.
The shield-block hit clip suits the role.
Armor, tabard, and eye variants with three presets: drowned, blackguard, ancient.
issues: The eye glow is a flat salmon orange; the mockup has a hot yellow center.
The skull is wide with thin tooth lines; the mockup skull is narrower with big clear teeth.
The cheek plates are small (larger ones touched the sword), and a faint seam crosses the cape at mid-height. The hilt and vambraces touch the breastplate by up to 1 cm in some clips.
skeleton-knight.next: Give the eyes a yellow core, narrow the skull and enlarge the teeth, and hide the cape seam.

cultist.summary: A new P1 dungeon enemy on the bandit base (knee bones, seven clips): a small figure in a crimson hood and ankle-length robe with black bands, a dark face with two slanted glowing purple eyes, a bone skull charm, a curved ritual dagger in the right hand, and a black candle with a flickering purple flame in the left. The taunt is a chant with the candle raised. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The hood silhouette, dark face, and purple eyes read as the mockup cultist at a glance.
The candle stays upright in every clip and the flame follows the eye color slot.
Robe and eye variants with three presets: zealot, shade, mirecaller.
issues: The eyes are smaller and dimmer than in the mockup; at 128 px they are small spots.
The chibi arms are short, so the chant raises the candle only to eye level.
The hood makes a small ridge where it meets the collar, and the skull charm is small and simple.
cultist.next: Enlarge and brighten the eyes, smooth the hood into the shoulders, and enlarge the charm.

goblin-shaman.summary: A new P1 enemy on the goblin-archer base (knee bones, seven clips): a goblin shaman with a bone-and-feather headdress, cream face paint, a patched hide mantle and kilt, bead and tooth necklaces, and a crooked staff with a skull and a glowing green flame. attack is a cast where the flame flares; taunt shakes the staff and hops. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings. A second forge all completed every preset sprite.
strengths: The skull staff, green flame, headdress, face paint, and patched cloak read as the mockup shaman.
The cast attack flares the flame on its own bone.
Skin, cloak, and magic variants (the eyes follow the magic color) with three presets: hexer, firecaller, bogseer.
issues: The feathers read as narrow white blades from the front; the mockup feathers are broad, grey, and fanned.
The skin is brighter and more yellow-green than the mockup, and the mantle has no bunched collar.
goblin-shaman.next: Broaden and grey the feathers, darken the skin a little.

bandit-archer.summary: A new P1 enemy for forest and village roads on the bandit base, with the bow, string, arrow, and quiver built from the archer: a dark green hood and mantle, a grey cloth mask over the lower face, a brown leather vest with a quiver strap, a belt with pouches, a short bow, and a quiver. attack is the archer shot (nock, draw, hold, release); the taunt beckons and shakes the bow. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The hood, mask, vest, bow, and quiver read clearly at 128 px.
The shot clip reuses the archer rig, so the string and arrow behave correctly.
Hood (with mantle and tunic), vest, eye, and skin variants with three presets: poacher, raider, cutthroat.
issues: The hood is a brighter, more saturated green than the muted green of the mockup, and the mask is grey instead of beige.
The bow rests vertical at the side; the mockup holds it low and diagonal across the front.
The bow or string touches the tunic, vest, or mantle by up to 1.6 cm for short moments in run, attack, and death.
bandit-archer.next: Mute the hood green, make the mask beige, and hold the bow diagonally in the rest pose.

zombie-soldier.summary: A new P1 dungeon enemy on the zombie base (knee bones, seven clips): a bald grey-green cracked skull with one milky eye and one yellow eye, a wide grimace, a torn faded-teal tunic with a leather mantle, a cross strap, a belt with pouches, bracers, grey trousers, brown boots, and a notched rusty short sword in the right hand. The attack is a sword chop while the left hand grabs. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The head, the two different eyes, and the teal tunic read as the mockup at a glance.
The sword chop gives the attack a clear read.
Eye, skin, and clothing variants with three presets: deserter, bog, veteran.
issues: The leather mantle is a thick collar ring; the mockup has a large draped shoulder cape.
The mouth is small and reads weakly at 128 px.
30,796 triangles is heavy for a small enemy.
In the death clip the sword comes to the skin of the head (the check still passes).
next: Enlarge the shoulder cape on the left.
Make the mouth wider and darker.

vampire.summary: A new P1 dungeon enemy on the rogue base (knee bones, eight clips): a pale noble with slicked black hair and a widow's peak, big red eyes, small fangs, pointed ears, a high flared collar with a red lining, a black cape to the ground, a burgundy vest with gold buttons, and a white frilled cravat. The attack is a cape swirl and a biting lunge; the victory is a cape spread with a small hover. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The collar, cape, and red eyes read as a vampire at a glance, also at 128 px.
The attack and victory clips use the cape instead of a weapon.
Eye, hair, and clothing variants with three presets: count, elder, fledgling; the cape and collar linings follow the clothing slot.
issues: The hair is a smooth dome; the mockup has larger wavy locks.
The cravat is a long narrow frill; the mockup has a fuller bow.
In attack2 the white cuffs go about 1 cm into the capelet.
next: Give the hair two or three larger locks.
Make the cravat shorter and fuller.

ghoul.summary: A new P1 dungeon enemy on the goblin-warrior base (knee bones, seven clips): a lean pale grey-violet ghoul with very long pointed ears, big pale-yellow eyes under angry brows, a wide grin with two rows of pointed teeth, a pot belly, thin arms with long three-fingered claws, clawed feet, and torn rags at the waist. The attack is a two-handed claw rake; the taunt is a hop with a cackle. The build has no warnings.
strengths: The ears, eyes, and toothy grin read as the mockup at a glance and at 128 px.
The claw rake gives the attack a clear read without a weapon.
Skin, eye, and rag variants with three presets: bog, crypt, butcher.
issues: The mockup ghoul is stockier, with thicker thighs and more rib detail.
The ears spread to the sides; the mockup ears stand up and cup forward.
The hands hang close to the body; the rags hang higher than in the mockup.
next: Tilt the ears up and forward.
Widen the stance and thicken the thighs.

wraith.summary: A new P1 dungeon enemy on the ghost base (floating rig, six clips): a big slate hood around a black void with two pale-blue glowing eyes, a capelet with a tie knot and cords, drooping sleeves with a large bony claw on the right and a bony left hand holding a rusty cage lantern with a blue flame, and ragged strips that reach the floor. The attack is a reaching claw with a lantern swing. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The hood, the void face, and the blue eyes read as a wraith at a glance.
The lantern glass and flame follow the eye color slot.
Cloak and glow variants with three presets: dusk, bog, grave.
issues: The strips are round ribbons that spread on the floor, so they read a little like tentacles; the mockup strips are thin, frayed, and hang straight.
The capelet is smooth; the mockup has a thick bunched cowl.
The mockup also shows a tall blue flame above the lantern.
next: Make the strips thinner and flatter, hanging straight down.
Bunch the capelet into a lumpy cowl.

necromancer.summary: A new P1 dungeon enemy on the cultist base (knee bones, seven clips): a black hood with a curled tip over a pale grey-green face with heavy brows and big glowing green eyes, a black robe open over a dark green under-robe, bone-white star patches, a bone buckle, a small skull shoulder pad, and a wooden staff with a skull and a flickering green flame. The attack raises the staff, flares the flame, and casts forward. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The hood, the green eyes, and the skull staff read as a necromancer at a glance and at 128 px.
The flame follows the eye color slot and flares in the attack.
Robe, under-robe, and eye variants with three presets: gravecaller, bloodbinder, frostwight.
issues: The mockup hood is taller and more tapered with a deeper opening.
The robe is compact; the mockup has bell sleeves, more folds, and a wider hem.
The staff is in the character's left hand (the mockup's viewer-right); in the attack the lower staff goes about 1 cm into the robe.
next: Make the hood taller and more pointed.
Widen the sleeves and the hem.

stone-golem.summary: A new P1 dungeon enemy on the minotaur-guard base (knee bones, eight clips): a stocky golem of grey chiseled stone blocks with moss on the tops, huge shoulder boulders, big block fists, glowing blue eyes, and a glowing blue rune plate on the chest, over a sage-green stone core. The attack is a two-fist ground slam. The build has no warnings.
strengths: The blocky stone silhouette, moss, and blue glow read as a stone golem at 128 px.
The two-fist slam reads clearly.
Stone and glow variants with three presets: desert, deep, ember.
issues: The sage-green core shows between the stones, so the body reads greener than the grey mockup.
The rocks are rounded stacked boxes; the mockup has more sharp-edged plates.
The head is a smooth dome; the mockup head looks like a helmet with cheek plates. 48k triangles.
next: Make the core grey so only the moss is green.
Add sharper plates and a helmet-like brow.

death-knight.summary: A new P1 dungeon enemy on the skeleton-knight base (knee bones, seven clips): a closed black horned helmet with glowing icy-blue visor eyes, black spiked plate with a cold sheen, a purple knit layer and scarf, a tattered purple cape to the ground, and a broad black greatsword with five glowing rune glyphs. The attack is a two-handed overhead chop. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The horns, visor eyes, and runed greatsword read as a death knight at a glance and at 128 px.
The overhead chop is clear and the sword never touches the head or horns.
Cloth and glow variants with three presets: nightfall, bloodsworn, plaguebound.
issues: The mockup shows a grey face with big round eyes under an open helmet; this helmet is closed with a slit, as asked.
The helmet is taller and egg-shaped, without cheek guards.
In the chop the forearms go up to 6 cm into the breastplate (short chibi arms).
next: Add cheek guards and lower the helmet crown.
Widen the cape at the front sides.

bone-golem.summary: A new P1 dungeon enemy on the stone-golem base (knee bones, eight clips): a big angry skull with a jaw and glowing red eyes, two shoulder skulls, an open rib cage over a dark hollow, bundled arm bones ending in knuckle-bone club fists, lumpy leg bones with blocky feet, riveted iron bands at the wrists, waist, and shins, and a rust leather belt plate. The attack is the two-fist ground slam. The build has no warnings.
strengths: The skull, red eyes, rib cage, and shoulder skulls read as a bone golem at a glance.
The iron bands give a clear value contrast against the cream bones.
Bone, glow, and band variants with three presets: ashen, crypt, ancient.
issues: 74,856 triangles is very heavy for one enemy.
The skull is rounder than the mockup's heavy-browed skull.
The shoulder skulls sit high, so part of the upper arm shows below them; the fists are closed clubs, not open bony hands.
next: Cap the triangle count per body.
Lower the shoulder skulls against the jaw and add a heavier brow.

paladin.summary: A new P1 hero on the knight base (the rogue's face and proportions, knee bones, eight clips): a young blond paladin with a bare head, silver plate with gold trim, a white tabard with a raised gold sun, a V hem with a gold diamond, a blue cowl and long cape, a silver war hammer with gold rings in the right hand, and a heater shield with a gold sun on the left arm. The attack is an overhead hammer strike. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The face, hair, and white-and-gold tabard read as a bright paladin at a glance and at 128 px.
It matches the P0 hero set: same head construction and proportions as the rogue and knight.
Eye, hair, cloth, and tabard variants with three presets: dawn, crusader, warden.
issues: The hair is a rounded cap; the mockup has bigger separate curls over the forehead.
The hammer rests low (fist at belt height); the mockup holds it at chest height.
The shield is a heater shield like the knight's, not the round shield of the text; no mail between the plates.
next: Split the hair into two or three larger curls.
Raise the hammer arm in the rest pose.

ranger.summary: A new P1 hero on the archer base (the rogue's face and proportions, knee bones, eight clips): a young ranger with a forest-green hood up, auburn hair, green eyes, a green capelet with a gold clasp, a long open cloak, a brown leather jerkin with a belt, cross-strap, and pouch, green bracers, tall boots, a longbow in the left hand, and a quiver worn over the cloak. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The hood, hair, and bow read as a ranger at a glance and at 128 px.
It matches the P0 hero set: same head construction and proportions as the rogue and archer.
Eye, hair, skin, and cloak variants with three presets: dusk, wanderer, warden.
issues: The mockup holds the bow across the body in both hands; the ranger holds it upright like the archer.
The mockup tunic under the capelet is green; this one is a brown leather jerkin.
The bow goes 1 to 2 cm into the jerkin in the attacks, as on the archer.
next: Consider a two-hand bow rest pose for the idle clip.

monk.summary: A new P1 hero on the rogue base (knee bones, eight clips): a young monk with a shaved head and a small top knot, an orange wrap robe with saffron collar bands and bell sleeves, a brown sash with a bow, wooden prayer beads, wide trousers, striped hand and shin wraps, and sandals. The attack is a palm strike; attack2 is a jumping spin kick; victory is a salute and a bow. The build has no warnings.
strengths: The shaved head, top knot, and saffron robe read as a monk at a glance and at 128 px.
Unarmed clips (palm strike, spin kick, salute) fit the role; the skirt follows the legs in the kick.
Eye, skin, and robe variants with three presets: temple, mountain, novice.
issues: The arms hang at the sides; the mockup holds them out, and its hands are bigger.
The cuff edges are a little jagged in close renders.
The underskirt is a thin band; the mockup has a wide yellow underlayer and a pointed front flap.
next: Give the idle clip a ready stance with the arms out.
Enlarge the hands a little.

barbarian.summary: A new P1 hero on the knight base (the rogue's face construction, knee bones, eight clips): a young barbarian with a wild red mane, a top knot and a side braid, a grey fur mantle and cape, bare arms with blue paint bands, leather bracers, a chest strap, a studded leather kilt with a round bronze buckle, fur-cuffed boots, and a double-bladed axe. The attack is a two-handed overhead chop; attack2 a horizontal sweep. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The red mane, fur, kilt, and double axe read as a barbarian at a glance and at 128 px.
It matches the hero set: same young face and proportions as the rogue and knight.
Hair, eye, skin, and paint variants with three presets: highlander, ember, wildwood.
issues: The mane is a tall round dome; the mockup mane is wider with a bigger top tuft.
The fur cape is a plain grey bell; the mockup fur sits mostly on the left shoulder, with big boot cuffs.
The paint is thin bands; the mockup has a larger arm tattoo and two crossed chest straps.
next: Widen the mane at the sides.
Move the fur toward the left shoulder and enlarge the boot cuffs.

bard.summary: A new P1 hero on the rogue base (knee bones, eight clips): a young bard with curly brown hair, a wide teal cap with a gold badge and a big red plume, a teal doublet with gold buttons, puffed sleeves and gold cuffs, a short dark cape, and a ribbed wooden lute held across the body. The attack is a strum that sends a glowing gold note; attack2 swings the lute; victory strums and hops. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The cap with the red plume and the lute read as a bard at a glance and at 128 px.
The glowing note gives the attack a clear read without a weapon.
Hair, eye, skin, and clothing variants with three presets: troubadour, minstrel, wanderer.
issues: 61,684 triangles; the lute strings alone are 11k.
The cap brim is flat like a sun hat; the mockup brim turns up at the front.
The cape is short and narrow; the mockup cape flares wide and nearly reaches the ground.
next: Cap the string triangles.
Turn up the front of the brim and lengthen the cape.

mage.summary: A new P1 hero on the wizard base (knee bones, eight clips): a young beardless mage with silver hair and round black glasses, a tall deep-blue hat with raised silver stars and a hooked point, a blue robe with silver bands over a grey under-robe, a blue cowl and cape, a belt with a pouch, a short wand with a glowing blue flame, and a red spellbook on the left palm. The attack is a wand flick; attack2 fires the flame as a bolt. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The starred hat, glasses, and glowing wand read as a mage at a glance and at 128 px.
It keeps the hero set's young face while matching the mockup's outfit.
Eye, hair, skin, and robe variants with three presets: arcanist, tidecaller, sage.
issues: 65,640 triangles is heavy.
The robe has narrow silver bands and no wide grey side panels; the hat hook curls less than in the mockup.
The wand and flame are small.
next: Cap the triangle count.
Enlarge the wand flame a little.

priest.summary: A new P1 hero on the cleric base with the rogue's human face and proportions (knee bones, eight clips): a young priest with dark swept hair, a long white robe with bell sleeves, a gold yoke, a gold stole with a cross and fringe, a wooden staff with a gold sunburst in the right hand, and a small book with a gold cross in the left. The attack raises the staff and bursts a glowing star; attack2 is a book blessing. The forge check shows result ok, and the build has no warnings.
strengths: The white and gold vestments and the sun staff read as a priest at a glance and at 128 px.
It matches the hero set's young face and proportions.
Hair, eye, skin, and trim variants with three presets: moon, martyr, pilgrim.
issues: The hair is a round mushroom shape; the mockup has sharper wave locks.
The white collar at the neck does not show.
The sleeves are thinner and less puffy than in the mockup.
next: Add two or three wave locks to the hair.

wood-golem.summary: Wood golem reworked 2026-09-30 by a Sonnet 5.5 high-tier agent in three passes (120,760 tokens), from 3.8 to 7.5: glowing amber eye slits and a flower-sigil core, darker lumpy moss on paler planks with dark seams, a seven-stave crown fan, arm plank seams, root grooves and rope wraps on the shins, root-clump feet, five vines. 70,148 triangles, no warnings, ground ok. Still below the 8 bar; the source stays uncommitted (untracked, owned by the dungeon denizens session).
strengths: The crown fan, vines, and rope wraps break the outline in every sprite direction.
The core sigil reads at 128 px and in the three-quarter view.
Materials now separate: pale planks, near-black seams, dark moss, tan rope.
issues: The eye slits show only as small amber flecks in the S, SW, and SE sprites; the brow shades them at the sprite camera angle.
The head is a stack of gapped slabs, not carved wavy billets.
The arms are smooth staves with faint seams.
next: Raise the eye slot 0.02 and push the slits to z 0.12 so the brow does not shade them.
Carve two wavy billets into the face planks.

samurai.summary: A new P1 hero on the paladin base (the knight's body, the rogue's face, knee bones, eight clips), built by a Sonnet 5.5 subagent in two passes: a red lacquer kabuto with a black lacquer bowl, gold rivets, a thick gold crescent crest and gold side fins, a black topknot, a red scale cuirass with dark scale rows over indigo sleeves and hakama, a red cord sash, red forearm guards, red sandals, a katana rigid in the right hand, and a wakizashi at the left hip. Attack is a horizontal slash, attack2 an overhead cut. 49,672 triangles, no build warnings, forge check result ok.
strengths: The black bowl, gold crescent, and red cuirass give three clear value masses, so the head reads at 128 px in all eight directions.
It matches the P0 hero set: the same head construction, face, and proportions as the knight and paladin, beardless as the set requires.
The dark scale rows follow the armor tint, so the black, green, and indigo lacquer presets keep the pattern.
The attack clips keep the grip and bracers clear of the cuirass, and the katana never crosses the head.
issues: The crest tips are flatter than the mockup's steep horns; steeper horns would break the 0.95 m height.
The neck guard is a plain bucket from the back.
The gold rivets on the bowl are too small to read at 128 px.
The death clip still reports small body contact: 1.3 cm for the katana fitting and 0.8 cm for the left hand on the wakizashi.
next: Raise the crest tips by 2 cm and accept a 0.97 m height, or shorten the topknot to keep the height.
Add two or three lame plates to the neck guard so the back view is not a plain dome.
Move the left hand off the wakizashi in the death clip.

orc-archer.summary: Orc archer on the orc warrior base: bald head with a topknot, small tusks, a dark jerkin with a quiver strap, two belts, a flat longbow across the body, and a quiver of arrows. Built by a Sonnet 5.5 high-tier agent in three passes (186,751 tokens).
strengths: The bow and quiver give a clear ranged silhouette in all eight sprite directions.
The tusks, topknot, and yellow eyes read at 128 px.
Clearance check ok; the draw hand clears the jerkin in attack.
issues: The skin renders a saturated green even with a dark base.
The collar notches are hidden by the jaw from the front.
The bowstring is static and does not follow the draw hand.
next: Animate the bowstring with a bone on the draw hand.
Try a desaturated skin option for the forest preset.

goblin-king.summary: Goblin king, the Labyrinth boss, on the goblin warrior base: a wide grinning face with fangs and lowered brows, a five-point gold crown with a red gem between two ivory horns, a fur collar, a purple cape with shoulder flaps, crossed straps with a bone medallion over a studded vest, a big belly, a gold-buckled belt, a strip loincloth, and a bone club. Built by a Sonnet 5.5 high-tier agent in two passes (173,443 tokens).
strengths: The crown, ears, and club read in every sprite direction.
The grin and lowered brows make him a boss, not a cute warrior.
Clearance check ok; seven clips including two attacks.
issues: 1.04 m to the crown tip, a little under the 1.1 m target.
The crown points are plain cones.
The cape back is a smooth bag; no draped folds.
next: Add two crown side spikes with gems for a more ornate silhouette.
Fold the cape with two vertical drapes on the back.

orc-shaman.summary: Orc shaman on the orc warrior base: a hunched sage-green caster with a bushy grey beard and one tusk, white face paint, a horned hood with a skull on the brow and two barbed feathers, a shaggy fur mantle, a bead necklace, a hide skirt with a rope belt, and a gnarled staff with a glowing green skull and flame. Built by a Sonnet 5.5 high-tier agent in two passes (198,890 tokens).
strengths: The glowing skull staff and the feathers give a tall, unmistakable silhouette in every sprite direction.
The beard, mantle, and hide read as three materials.
Clearance check ok; eight clips; sprites for the default and three presets.
issues: The hood still reads as a cap from the front.
The white face paint is faint at 128 px.
The staff wrap is thin; attack2 is a one-hand slam.
next: Raise the paint contrast or widen the band one more step.
Braid the staff wrap with a bump pattern.

ogre-brute.summary: Ogre brute on the orc warrior base scaled 1.25: a round-bellied tan ogre with a small tusked face in a dark mane, three-band bracers with red wraps, a rope belt with a tassel, a strip loincloth, and a big spiked club with a hanging rope toggle. Built by a Sonnet 5.5 high-tier agent in three passes (about 250,000 tokens). Below the 8 bar; the source is left uncommitted for the owner's call.
strengths: The belly, club, and tusks read at 128 px in every direction.
Clearance check ok, eight clips, sprites for the default and presets.
issues: The hanging left arm reaches the loincloth hem and reads stiff (the chibi arm length on a 1.3 m body).
The belly gradient and pec bulges are faint in the render.
The left hand stops short of the haft in the two-hand attack.
next: Bend the hanging arm at the elbow and turn the fist inward.
Paint the belly and pecs with a stronger value step, not a hue step.

dark-knight.summary: Horned dark knight on the knight base: brow band, cheek plates and crest on the helm, red visor glow, purple wing panels and trim, tabard emblem, ragged red cape, short blocky sword. Reviewed 8.0 after one feedback pass.
strengths: Silhouette matches the mockup in all four views: horns, crest, pauldrons, cape.
Sprites read horns, crest, red visor and cape at 128 px.
Clearance and ground checks pass; 43,730 triangles, no warnings.
issues: The chest reads more purple than the mockup's grey-violet.
The resting sword tip sits close to the ground in the front view.
dark-knight.next: Optional: desaturate the wing panels one step; raise the rest grip a few degrees.
